title: Context Estimation Accuracy — 2.4x Overestimate on Wakeup
summary: Wakeup protocol estimated 57% context usage (114KB), actual measured 23% (46KB). Estimation method is too naive and breaks transparency.
description: Session 73 wakeup briefing estimated context at 57% by summing file sizes without accounting for: (1) lazy-loaded content (lugs listed but not read), (2) compression efficiency (tokens ≠ file bytes), (3) truncated preview loads (WAI-State.md showed 73KB but only 2KB loaded). When user ran /context, actual was 23% — 2.4x error.
implications: Briefing context health reports are unreliable — breaks user trust in capacity warnings
YELLOW/ORANGE alerts may fire incorrectly, pushing premature closeouts
Framework appears imprecise when context health is core value prop
root_cause: Wakeup protocol Step 7 (Display Briefing) estimates budget by guessing file sizes. Should instead: (a) NOT estimate at all and just report measured state, or (b) use Claude's actual token counting, or (c) track cumulative tokens from each file load.
recommended_fix: Option A (safest): Remove token estimation from wakeup briefing. Report measured context from last session + note 'Run /context for live measurement' instead of predicting.
Option B (medium): Integrate /context measurement into wakeup Step 7. Call it before generating briefing to get actual usage.
Option C (future): Build lightweight token counter into wakeup that tracks each loaded file's actual consumption.
affected_lugs: epic-skill-thrift-v1 (Tier 1) — part of broader slim-down effort
next_action: Update wakeup protocol Step 7 (Context Budget Governor) — replace estimation with measured reality
learning: AI context measurement needs ground truth, not inference. Trust tool outputs (Claude's /context) over calculated estimates.
scope_verified_by: user feedback (Session 73: context estimation is framework-wide issue)
routing_notes: High-impact learning (impact: 9) that affects all spokes' wakeup protocol. Should be delivered to hub as framework teaching.
